next_steps.description: Kill or gracefully suspend non-essential sessions (e.g., ps5-hive, opencode) to free memory and CPU.

Instrument each active session (build_monitor, hive-dev, hive-live, hive-watch, nextjs-prod, opencode, orchestrator, ps5-hive, supervisor) with standardized health/metrics endpoints and log correlation IDs.

Add /api/metrics endpoint to pages/api/metrics.ts returning JSON of session stats (activeSessions, model, uptime, errors) aggregated from runtime state.
Apply stricter cgroup limits and lower niceness for research_loop jobs to reduce core contention.
Define per-session SLOs and backpressure rules (CPU/mem thresholds, queue depths) and wire them to hive-live for automated hysteresis scaling.
Write unit tests for org_guard.py covering all forbidden path patterns and escalation bypasses.

Create a controlled rollout policy for nextjs-prod including canary weights, automated smoke checks, and instant rollback triggers on error-rate or latency breaches.
Add /api/metrics endpoint to logstream.py returning JSON of session stats (sessions, throughput, errors).

learned.description: Injects max_tasks, max_hours, and task_timeout guardrails into hive config and respawns the session to prevent unbounded retries and enforce controlled shutdown.
learned.example: grep -q '^max_tasks=' ~/.hive/config || echo 'max_tasks=1000' >> ~/.hive/config && grep -q '^max_hours=' ~/.hive/config || echo 'max_hours=48' >> ~/.hive/config && grep -q '^task_timeout=' ~/.hive/config || echo 'task_timeout=7200' >> ~/.hive/config && tmux respawn-window -t SESSION

learned.description: Detects and force-clears port collisions then verifies bind before respawning dependent tmux windows.
learned.example: ss -tlnp | grep PORT && lsof -ti:PORT | xargs -r kill -9; sleep 1; python3 -c "import socket; s=socket.socket(); s.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1); s.bind(('', PORT)); print('bind ok'); s.close()" && tmux respawn-window -t SESSION

learned.description: Safely injects missing config keys and applies them via window respawn to avoid stale state.
learned.example: grep -q task_timeout ~/.hive/config || echo 'task_timeout=7200' >> ~/.hive/config && tmux respawn-window -t SESSION
